prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 — key policies (ideology-free summary)

Economy, business, trade and skills
- Responsible public finances; restore stability with independent OBR forecasts and Bank of England independence.
- Repair EU ties to cut trade barriers; seek veterinary/plant health and mutual recognition agreements; aim to join the Single Market longer term.
- Green industrial strategy; expand British Business Bank; abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy.
- Tax changes: restore bank surcharge/levy, raise Digital Services Tax to 6%, reform capital gains tax, 4% levy on FTSE-100 share buybacks; priority future cut by raising personal allowance when affordable.
- Replace apprenticeship levy with a flexible skills levy; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aim £10,000); boost apprenticeships and careers advice.
- AI: cross-sector regulatory framework; join US–EU Trade and Technology Council.

Climate, energy and environment
- Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; no fracking or new coal.
- Ten-year home upgrade: insulation and heat pumps (free for low-income); zero‑carbon standard for new buildings; social energy tariff; decouple electricity prices from gas.
- Expand storage, interconnectors and grid; support community energy; carbon border adjustment.
- End sewage discharges: tougher regulator, “Sewage Tax,” real-time data, binding targets; transform water firms to public benefit companies.
- Nature targets (“double nature” by 2050); 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; deposit return scheme; phase out non‑recyclable single-use plastics.

Health and social care
- Right to see a GP within 7 days (24 hours urgent); recruit 8,000 GPs; expand pharmacists’ roles; universal 24/7 booking.
- NHS dentistry access via contract reform; urgent care guarantees; supervised toothbrushing and VAT cut on children’s dental products.
- Mental health: walk‑in hubs for young people; check‑ups at key life stages; one qualified professional in every school; end out-of-area placements.
- Cancer: 100% start treatment within 62 days; replace ageing radiotherapy; more cancer nurses; faster approvals.
- Workforce plan, independent pay review; 10‑year capital plan; interoperable digital records.
- Drug policy: health-led approach; expand treatment; legal, regulated cannabis market (18+).
- Social care: free personal care; Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hr); Royal College of Care Workers; paid carer’s leave and respite; National Care Agency.

Education, families and young people
- Mental health professional in every school; per‑pupil funding rising above inflation; repair unsafe buildings.
- Tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils; SEND national body and extra funding.
- Early years: extra free hours for disadvantaged 3–4s; triple Early Years Pupil Premium.
- Reinstate university maintenance grants; Student Mental Health Charter; rejoin Erasmus+; Horizon Europe/EIC participation.
- Parental leave/pay: day‑one rights incl. self‑employed; double Statutory Maternity and Shared Parental Pay to £350/week; paternity at 90% (capped); extra use‑it‑or‑lose‑it month; paid neonatal leave.
- Free school meals for all children in poverty (ambition: all primary).

Welfare and pensions
- Remove two‑child limit and benefit cap; reduce Universal Credit wait to 5 days; scrap bedroom tax; replace sanctions with incentive‑based support.
- End deep poverty target; independent commission on UC adequacy.
- Protect pension triple lock; address gender pension gap; fair compensation for 1950s-born women.
- Increase and widen Carer’s Allowance eligibility.

Crime, policing and justice
- Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance and investigation of all burglaries.
- New Online Crime Agency; properly resource NCA; scrap PCCs for local Police Boards.
- Halve time from offence to sentencing; tackle court backlogs; expand restorative justice.
- VAWG: specialist support, mandatory trauma training; domestic abuse specialists in police control rooms.
- Youth diversion nationwide; stronger fraud protections and bank reimbursement.

Housing and local government
- Build 380,000 homes/year, including 150,000 social; 10 new garden cities; reform land compensation (current‑use value).
- Ban no‑fault evictions; default three‑year tenancies; national landlord register.
- Abolish leasehold; cap ground rents; remove dangerous cladding at no cost to leaseholders; rent‑to‑own for social housing.
- End rough sleeping; stronger local powers over second homes/short‑lets; gigabit broadband for all.

Transport
- Accelerate EV transition: charging rollout, plug‑in grant, 2030 zero‑emission sales restored, 5% VAT on public charging, card access.
- Freeze rail fares; new Railway Agency; electrification programme; Northern Powerhouse Rail; expand bus franchising; nationwide active travel; shift road budget to maintenance.

Immigration and asylum
- End Hostile Environment; move work/student visa policy to relevant departments.
- Scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme; uphold Refugee Convention; safe/legal routes (expanded resettlement, humanitarian travel permits, wider family reunion).
- Clear asylum backlog with 3‑month service standard; right to work after 3 months; time‑limit adult detention (28 days); end child detention.
- Merit‑based work visas; exempt NHS/care from skills charge and allow dependants; expand Youth Mobility; reverse family visa income hike.
- EU citizens: automatic Settled Status, physical proof; reduce child citizenship fee; implement Windrush review; repeal Right to Rent; legal‑aid expansion.

Rights, equality and political reform
- Uphold Human Rights Act and ECHR; Digital Bill of Rights; regulate biometric surveillance.
- Make misogyny a hate crime; ban conversion practices; protect reproductive rights.
- Disability employment and Access to Work reforms; UNCRPD into UK law.
- Electoral reform: PR (STV) for MPs and English councils; votes at 16; cap donations; stronger transparency; reform House of Lords; federal UK with enhanced devolution; citizens’ assemblies.

Defence and international
- Increase defence spending yearly (ambition 2.5% of GDP); reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; tighter arms export controls; parliamentary vote before military action.
- Strengthen European security cooperation; seek EU defence/security agreement; back NATO and Ukraine; seize Russian assets to support Ukraine.
- Restore aid to 0.7% GNI with poverty focus; climate and education priorities.
- Middle East: immediate bilateral ceasefire, two‑state solution, recognise Palestine; proscribe Iran’s IRGC.
- Support BNO Hong Kongers; recognise Uyghur genocide; fund BBC World Service.
